Thanks for a great call this morning — appreciate you walking through Redwood's serving model. A few clarifying points from our side so we can scope the POC: 

- SLO target: we'd like p95 latency under 350ms for single-turn inference (text-in -> text-out) at expected concurrency of ~40 qps.
- Throughput/Concurrency: baseline is 40 qps sustained with spikes to 110 qps during batch processing windows.
- Context: typical user requests are short (100-300 input tokens) but we need to support multi-message threads — worst-case input + expected assistant output approaches ~6,500 tokens.
- Streaming: for UX we want partial output streaming for longer responses; intermittent streaming is OK.

Can Redwood confirm whether a 6.5k token envelope (input+output combined) will materially change the p95 projection you gave on the call? Also: what are the sandbox/POC steps to validate at our concurrency profile?

Tom — thanks for the clear summary and the sketch, that helps a lot. Below are concrete notes from our engineering side and proposed POC steps. I've kept each item short and actionable.

1) Latency impact vs token envelope
- Small requests (<=512 tokens total): we expect p95 ~120–180ms on our hosted SKU with 1x dedicated inference slab for the model band discussed.
- Large envelopes (~6.5k tokens): cost and latency grow quasi-linearly for generation-heavy outputs because of autoregressive decoding and KV-cache handling. In our internal tests, 6k total tokens pushes p95 to ~900–1,200ms on a single-node baseline without streaming.
- Mitigations: streaming generation reduces perceived latency (first-token times) significantly — first-token p50 can be <200ms while full-sequence p95 remains above target depending on output length. Prefix/KV caching helps if many requests share common history.

2) Throughput and concurrency hedges
- For sustained 40 qps with occasional 110 qps spikes we recommend a two-slab config for the POC (primary slab sized for 60 qps sustained + auto-burst to a second slab during peak).
- Autoscaling latency: with our default scale policy cold-start for additional slabs is ~30–45s; we recommend using our burst pool or pre-warming before scheduled windows.

3) Streaming requirements
- Streaming supported. For your UX we suggest starting with chunked streaming for outputs >256 tokens so users see early content. This gives you first-byte latencies in the 150–300ms range for typical prompts.

4) POC plan (proposed timeline)
- Day 0–2: Exchange three representative prompt sets (short, medium, long) + sample production traffic sketch.
- Day 3–5: Redwood config & baseline run (single-node), focused on p50/p95 with and without streaming.
- Day 6–10: Scale tests (sustained 40 qps, spike to 110 qps) + failure/fallback scenarios.
- Deliverable: perf report + recommended slab sizing and cost estimate.

Action items for Finlytics: please confirm three representative prompts (short/med/long) and whether you want streaming enabled for the initial run. Also confirm whether encryption-at-rest/KMS reqs should be included in the POC build.

I've attached a short runbook stub (redwood-runbook-stub.md) with our proposed metrics to collect during the POC. Marissa / Ben — feel free to jump in on sizing/cost details.

Thanks,
